parsed.study_design: Exploratory case-based commentary using secondary sources
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents, Adivasis, farmers, and landless or land-poor households in Plachimada, Kerala; no defined sample
parsed.exposure: Coca-Cola groundwater extraction and waste disposal within a regulatory context involving panchayat licensing, state permissions, water law, courts, and pollution-control authorities
parsed.outcome: Groundwater depletion, dry irrigation wells, reduced agricultural production, contamination concerns, and community exclusion from water and governance rights
parsed.rationale: The Plachimada section reports access-relevant consequences—lowered groundwater levels, dry wells, and reduced harvests—alongside licensing and governance disputes (pp. 642–645). However, the author calls the article “very exploratory and quite incomplete” and states that the case account is gleaned from multiple secondary sources rather than reporting an identifiable empirical method, sampling strategy, or systematic synthesis (p. 640; note 3, p. 654). It is therefore excluded as commentary without original or systematically synthesized empirical evidence.
